title: Jesus before Pilate Part 3
scripture_text: ‘’Then the Jewish leaders took Jesus from Caiaphas to the palace of the Roman governor. By now it was early morning, and to avoid ceremonial uncleanness they did not enter the palace, because they wanted to be able to eat the Passover. So Pilate came out to them and asked, “What charges are you bringing against this man?” “If he were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed him over to you.” Pilate said, “Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.” “But we have no right to execute anyone,” they objected. This took place to fulfil what Jesus had said about the kind of death he was going to die. Pilate then went back inside the palace, summoned Jesus and asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” “Is that your own idea,”Jesus asked, “or did others talk to you about me?” “Am I a Jew?” Pilate replied. “Your own people and chief priests handed you over to me. What is it you have done?” Jesus said, “My kingdom is not of this world. If it were, my servants would fight to prevent my arrest by the Jewish leaders. But now my kingdom is from another place.” “You are a king, then!” said Pilate. Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. In fact, the reason I was born and came into the world is to testify to the truth. Everyone on the side of truth listens to me.” “What is truth?” retorted Pilate. With this he went out again to the Jews gathered there and said, “I find no basis for a charge against him. But it is your custom for me to release to you one prisoner at the time of the Passover. Do you want me to release ‘the king of the Jews’?” They shouted back, “No, not him! Give us Barabbas!” Now Barabbas had taken part in an uprising. Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged. The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head. They clothed him in a purple robe and went up to him again and again, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” And they slapped him in the face. Once more Pilate came out and said to the Jews gathered there, “Look, I am bringing him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against him.” When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!” As soon as the chief priests and their officials saw him, they shouted, “Crucify! Crucify!” But Pilate answered, “You take him and crucify him. As for me, I find no basis for a charge against him.” The Jewish leaders insisted, “We have a law, and according to that law he must die, because he claimed to be the Son of God.” When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid, and he went back inside the palace. “Where do you come from?” he asked Jesus, but Jesus gave him no answer. “Do you refuse to speak to me?” Pilate said. “Don’t you realize I have power either to free you or to crucify you?” Jesus answered, “You would have no power over me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you is guilty of a greater sin.” From then on, Pilate tried to set Jesus free, but the Jewish leaders kept shouting, “If you let this man go, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who claims to be a king opposes Caesar.” When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judge’s seat at a place known as the Stone Pavement (which in Aramaic is Gabbatha). It was the day of Preparation of the Passover; it was about noon.“Here is your king,”Pilate said to the Jews. But they shouted, “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!” “Shall I crucify your king?” Pilate asked. “We have no king but Caesar,” the chief priests answered. Finally Pilate handed him over to them to be crucified.’’
devotional:
Pilate was a man who was motivated by fear.

John tells us in John 19v8 that ‘he (Pilate) was even more afraid.’

This is very interesting. Pilate feared the Jewish leaders in case they reported him to Caesar. They said to Pilate. ‘If you let this man go you are no friend of Caesar.

‘Friend of Caesar' was a coveted title of honour given by the Emperor for service. The title implied the recipient had a personal relationship with the Caesar, and so, had political clout. For Pilate, the title would have meant an appointment to a much more desirable post than Judea.

His motivation was fear and self-protection. He did not care what principles he had to break, or what morals he would have to ditch as long as he could hold unto his position of power. He feared loosing something that was not worth having.

Pilate refuses to take responsibility.

In three ways Pilate tries to get away from taking responsibility, [a] he tells the crowd to take Jesus and judge him John 18:31. Then he tells them to take Jesus and crucify Him. ‘As for me I find no basis for a charge against him.’ 19:6. [b] Luke tells us that Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Luke 23:6 [c] He washes his hand in a basin saying ‘I am innocent of this man’s blood, it is your responsibility.’ Matthew27:24.

Pontius Pilate, the governor, the most powerful man in the region, the only one with the judicial faculty to hand a man over to death, stands before a crowd and claims that he is not responsible for what he does. He claims that, in violating his own conscience and handing over an innocent man to torture, he is innocent.

‘It’s not my fault, he is to blame, I couldn’t help it, I didn’t mean to hurt him.’ People have lots of different ways of avoiding taking responsibilities. Maybe there has been a ‘Pilate’ in you life, someone at home, at work, at church, at school, someone who has misused their position to hurt you. Jesus knows how you feel, Jesus has stood where you stand and He understands the pain you have experienced.

Looking at Pilate, we do not see a very nice person, he is a miserable human being with no redeeming qualities or moral courage, who uses his power for self gain and gratification.

However when we look at Jesus we see someone who with internal beauty and strength was able to handle the cruel injustices.

1. He refused to use his power and position for his own benefit. Reading about Jesus before Pilate, you wonder why Jesus would not just call down fire from heaven and show these people his power and strength? But he didn’t, why.

[a] In the garden he had completely and without reservation submitted himself to his Fathers will, and he knew that this particular suffering was part of his fathers will. On occasions Jesus avoided suffering. Once the people of his own town tried to throw him of a cliff in order to kill him, and he walked away. Problem with you and me is we don’t always know if our suffering is part of God’s will for us, or if they are the consequences of living in a fallen world. I don’t think it is too important to know, but what is important is that we live surrendered lives. Jesus could stand before Pilate because he had ‘kneeled’ in the garden.

[b] Jesus never used his power to serve his own needs, this something he learned in the wilderness when he was tempted by Satan. Satan wanted him to assert his power and turn stone into bread in order to feed his hunger, but he refused.

[c] I think another reason why Jesus may not have called fire down from heaven and use his divine power was because he knew that when we stand before ’our Pilate’ we could not do that. He wanted to teach us how to handle injustice.

[d] Above all Jesus wanted to fulfil his Fathers plan of salvation, and His through suffering he gave himself a ransom for many.

Jesus remembered who he was and why he came look at verse 37.

‘You are a king, then!’ said Pilate. Jesus answered. ‘You are right in saying I am a king. In fact for this reason I was born, and for this I came into the world, to testify to truth. Everyone on the side of truth listens to me,’

I think this may be the only recorded time Jesus refers to his birth. When some one suffers the injustice of power abuse by another person, they can feel worthless and insignificant. But like Jesus we have been born with significance, value and purpose.

Suffering injustice is an extremely lonely and painful experience, however injustice is not all powerful, even though it might feel that it is. It cannot rob a person of their value or their God give purpose. It can do a lot of terrible things but it cannot change the reason for your being. The pain of life cannot rob a person of purposes of God.

Just notice that the purposes of God are always consistent with the truth. If we go into error, or pretence, or denial or unreality, then you are not in the will of God. Pilate and Jesus were completely opposite. Jesus overcame power with truth.

One final thing Jesus did as he stood before Pilate, he redefined what a kingdom was. A kingdom is the authority which you live, and the kingdom determines how you live. Jesus said ‘my kingdom is not of this world.’ So how Jesus approached life was the antitheses to how Pilate did

Pilate’s kingdom was about power.

Jesus’ kingdom is about truth.

Pilate’s kingdom used force and violence.

Jesus’ kingdom is about love and grace.

Pilate’s kingdom was about taking the lives of others.

Jesus’ kingdom is about laying down His life for others.

Pilate’s kingdom was about saving yourself

Jesus’ kingdom is about saving others.
prayer: Father thank you for the majestic beauty of Jesus and his kingdom.
